payout_quote: Living with Type 2 Diabetes can make managing blood sugar an ongoing challenge. Researchers are evaluating an investigational injectable medication for adults living with Type 2 Diabetes. This Phase 2 clinical research study is evaluating the safety, tolerability, and effectiveness of an investigational medication compared with placebo in adults with Type 2 Diabetes. ... By participating in this study, you could receive: Compensation up to $2,750 for your time, travel, and meals. Study-related medication and medical care are provided at no cost.
steps: Open the Centricity Research participate page and locate the Type 2 Diabetes injectable-medication study.
Check eligibility (ages 18-75, diagnosed Type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 7.0%-10.0%, BMI 25-50, managing with diet/exercise alone or stable metformin for 3 months).
Receive compensation up to $2,750 for your time, travel, and meals.
catches: Only adults with Type 2 diabetes meeting specific criteria (HbA1c 7.0-10.0, BMI 25-50, stable weight and medication) qualify — not everyone qualifies.
The $2,750 is an 'up to' ceiling for time, travel, and meals.
This is a Phase 2 study of an investigational injectable medication versus placebo — real medical risks, and you could receive placebo.
The exact visit schedule is disclosed in informed consent; participation is voluntary and you may withdraw.
You must pass the study screening process (medical history review, labs/exams as required) to enroll; not everyone qualifies.
biggest_catch: Only adults with Type 2 diabetes meeting narrow criteria (HbA1c 7.0-10.0, BMI 25-50) qualify for this Phase 2 placebo-controlled injectable study — the $2,750 is a ceiling for your time, travel, and meals, and you could receive placebo with real medical risks.
eligibility: Adults 18-75 diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes; HbA1c 7.0%-10.0%; BMI 25-50; managing with diet/exercise alone or stable metformin for 3 months; stable body weight for 3 months.
timing: Compensation paid for time, travel, and meals over the course of the study.
